lines.text: The sprint is over, and the retro starts in ten minutes.
You want to know where the time actually went, task by task.
Everyone remembers the sprint differently, and memory is not data.
In Agent R Q, every task has its own timeline, recorded automatically.
Start to close, you see time spent working, time blocked, and time waiting on a human.
Open all twelve, and compare them side by side.
Then a pattern appears. Approvals always wait the longest on Fridays.
That is a team habit, not an agent problem, and habits can be changed.
Maybe approvals get batched on Thursday afternoon, before the weekend rush.
Bring real data to your retro, instead of a gut feeling.
Next sprint, check the same timelines again and see whether the habit changed.
Know exactly where the time goes, every single sprint.
When do your agents wait longest for you? Tell us your day of the week, or try it at Agent R Q dot com.
